text: Let me start by saying I am normally very good at installing screen protectors. So I had two tries at this application as they now come with two tubes of glue. I watched installation videos before even opening the box. I made sure my desk was level. The conditions couldn't have been more perfect. Then I got to the moment of truth, dropping the glass down over the glue. Much to my dismay, unlike all the videos I watched, a thousand little air bubbles exploded into the glue. So I pulled it off, cleaned it up, and gave it a second try. Same exact thing. Instead of letting $45 go completely to waste, I decided I could live with the remaining bubbles after letting it sit for a while. It looked horrible, but I decided it was better than nothing. After putting up with it for a couple weeks, I pulled it out of my pocket last night and the edge of the screen protector had shattered. No clue why, but that was that. So I start pulling it off, and it just turns into this horrible sticky mess of shattered glass and residue left on my phone. I cut my fingers pulling it off. Goo Gone luckily got the residue off my phone and it doesn't seem to have taken any damage from the horrible removal process. Now I've seen these installations go successfully on Youtube, so I know I just got unlucky, but unlike normal screen protectors where you end up with an air bubble or a piece of dust or something, this is just all or nothing. Absolutely not worth the $45 gamble.
title: If you like to gamble

text: So close, but fails at my key need. As a power bank to carry around in a bag for charging devices, this works as well as any other 2-port Anker power bank or other decently specced competitor, which is to say it is great. Unfortunately, it has a glaring flaw: it doesn't supply power to the two USB-A ports while it is charging. I frequent places in the world where wall power isn't consistently available. If this worked for through-charging, it would be perfect: fast charging via USB-C when power is available, and the ability to charge two devices plugged in to it while it still increasing its own charge. It doesn't do that, though. It doesn't even seem to enable used ports automatically when it stops being charged: Plugging a USB light into it while charging leaves the light "off" (actually very dimly glowing with what I imagine is the sensing current). Either unplugging the USB-C cable or the charger results in the same behavior, which is... no change. If I unplug or switch off the light and plug/switch on again, it works, of course. Hopefully this gets fixed in the next iteration. Until then, this is more frustrating for my needs than it is helpful. If I were back in the states I would return it. Until then I'm relying on my much older USB-A powerbank that takes longer to charge but will pass through charge to all of its ports whenever there's something plugged in to it.

text: I have purchased 3 quite different cases since acquiring my iPhone 12Pro. The first was the simple, grippy but only modestly protective apple case (yellow on the left.) A phone that doesn't ring on incoming calls was unacceptable, so I switched the Incipio Defender (two pieces, red and black). Wonderful protection but clumsy in the hand and the buttons on the side and bottom charging port were hard to actuate. Finally, on recommendation, I got the Gripzilla. It is indeed grippy and seems to offer good protection as well as easy access to buttons and charging port.
title: This third case is a keeper.

text: I like this case a lot. It's super cute. Pluses: --The gold is pretty and shimmery but not blinding bright or overly noticeable. --The bow is surprisingly durable. I expected it to get messed up almost immediately or fall off, but it looks great after a couple months. --The seams are all straight. --The material doesn't feel flimsy. --The magnet closure holds it closed very well. --The strap is strong enough that I feel comfortable holding it by just that. --The plastic that holds the phone in is snug but not too hard to pop your phone out of when needed. It also does not block any of the functionality of the screen, which I've had happen with other cases. --The camera cutout is large enough to let you easily clean your lens. Negatives: --The clasp that connects the strap to the case is too thick. I fold my case open and connect the magnet so it's essentially inside out and my phone is on the top. The thickness of the clasp prevents you from moving the strap so it is not folded between the case. I actually clipped mine on backwards so i could use the strap when my case is folded open and I'm using it. --The rubber coating along the inside edge of the case that covers the raw seam of material comes off almost immediately. It's not terribly noticeable after it comes off, but it is annoying that it happened within a week. I'd still buy this case again despite the above. Good quality, cute, functional.
title: Well made case with a couple drawbacks

text: I have another parabolic antenna that works great on AT&T bands 2/4. That is why I have it to penetrate the trees out where we live. I'm keeping it though, in hopes that when 5g comes out here, it can help with that. For those of you on LTE, stick with the previous gen Parabolic and Yagi offerings mature on the market. UPDATE 9 JAN 2020: I have now tested this where several other modems, including modems that support Band 66 and 71. This is a highly directional unit, but once aligned it works great. It pulled in Band 71 and the results were great, tripled my upload. Its not as forgiving as the 1900 LTE parabolic, or the other Yagis though on directional aim.
title: Hoping for better on 5g

text: I bought this to consolidate multiple devices that required USB power into one charging hub. Alexa, a 12W USB task light, and an Amazon cloud cam. My first reaction is it was a little bit to travel with, but actually when you consider everything it replaces, it’s actually not bad. Plus, in hotels you’re often struggling to find enough wall sockets to plug in all your chargers. So this is a really handy way to charge everything in one location using only a single wall plug. I was also really wanting a product that was either ETL or UL certified for safety purposes. There are a lot of really cheap devices that have no certifications at all, and you’ll find a scary review or two about it catching fire. This is ETL certified, so gives me some peace of mind. Highly recommended!

text: Okay, I bought three of these to work with two Samsung Infuses and one HTC inspire. All phones where At&t phones and I had all unlocked at mall cell phone service center. NET10 and StraightTalk are sister companies that share the same service center and tech support personnel. The only difference is NET10 cards can be bought in many different locations (eg, gas stations, best buys, radio shacks, CVS's, walgreens etc) Straight talk service cards can only be bought online or at walmarts. Same service. Straight talk is strictly t-mobile now, and Net10 is T-mobile and At&t. At&t works best in the charlotte, NC region. Very happy with this service towers these run off of. Data is very fast.

text: I had high hopes for this booster. Looking at all of these reviews, I could see that this booster was capable of a lot of improvement if you can set it up properly, but that is where the issues come in. I was setting this up in my mom's house which is out in the “middle of nowhere” and she gets very poor cell reception in certain rooms of her home (the bathroom, laundry room, etc.) which were additions to the home. Upon first setting this up, I thought it was done because all of the sudden, my cell reception was so much better. However, this needed to be rebooted and reset several times after the initial setup because it was dropping signals left and right. There is a troubleshooting section in the instructions, but it is even harder to read than the other sections! I have still yet to fix this and am in the process of connecting with customer service. For the time being while it was working, I can say that it worked well to penetrate walls. The walls between my mom's laundry room addition and the rest of her house are made of brick which is why I thought the cell coverage was initially so poor, but this seemed to work right through it. If your home is also made of brick or other seemingly impenetrable materials, I highly suggest getting something that guarantees wall-breaking coverage like this. Overall, I think this could work well if there were easier instructions to read and if the receiver was more reliable.
title: Huge improvement if you can get it to work

text: This is without question, the best Android phone I've ever owned. This is a big step up from an LG Spectrum which was a workhorse for me and was itself a pretty great device with a very nice display. It was beginning to show its age, and it was a pretty good battery charge consumer. The LG G2 is very very responsive; the display is excellent. It takes wonderful photos when set to IA mode. The battery life is fantastic... I can go a few days with ease on one charge. I'm using a wireless Qi charger (PowerBot PB1020) for my Verizon model (the other models don't have this) so I don't physically cycle the microSD connector needlessly. It charges fine through a TPU (TUDIA Ultra Slim) case. I hope wireless charging long-term doesn't negatively impact battery longevity. Bluetooth connectivity with my Sony Automobile Car Stereo is excellent. I can make and receive calls hands free. I can stream TuneIn and Pandora with no problems with the device. A nice program that comes with the phone is "Quick Remote"... My kids often misplace the TV or the Cable Box remotes. Ha - I can use my phone now to control these since the phone has a built-in IR transmitter. I find the LG Skin to be feature-rich, and you can tailor it to your liking; You can replace it all together if you desire. I think people need to get familiar with it and give it a chance before flat out replacing it with something downloaded from the PlayStore.
title: Excellent Product

text: I use an S3 with a Ballistic case. Overall I like this case. I've only had this for a week and have only one complaint. Too much Velcro! The approximately 3inch strip of hook and loop is excessive for keeping the flap shut. One has to hold down the body of the case with one hand and lift the flap with the other or you are holding the phone and the case in your hand off your belt or pocket. Fixed it by using my Dremel with a cutoff wheel. Holding the Dremel with the wheel perpendicular to the hooks, I lightly removed about a quarter of the length off of each end of the hook strip, being careful not to grind off the thread used to sew the strip on or through the base of the strip that the hooks are mounted to. text: I removed the 'white' sticky decal from the underside of the receiver. This made the receiver thinner so there was no budge once the back cover was snapped onto my phone. I also used clear packaging tape to fasten the receiver to the underside of my phones back cover. By doing this I am able to remove the back cover that have direct access to my phones battery, mini SD card and SIM card with out having to deal with the receiver fastened to the battery. The alteration also improved my NFC reception. The installation when like this, packaging tape placed upon the receiver surface which previously had the 'white' sticky decal. Lay the receiver onto the phone so that the metal charging contacts are ingaged to the phone. Place the back cover onto the phone snapping it all around. Press on the center of the battery cover so the clear packaging tape contacts the back cover. Remove the back cover which should have the receiver fastened to its underside. Make sure the clear packaging tape is totaly in contact with the phones cover. Replace the back cover to engage the wireless receiver and test for contact with the wireless pad. I found that the reception of my phone to the wireless pad much improved with this alteration. Should your phone not start charging then you will have to readjust the position of the receiver onto the inside of the back cover. I have posted a picture of the finished altered receiver on my back cover.

Bottom Line: If you appreciate the ultimate in afforded protection for your $300+ device, this case is for you. Also, the holes for the buttons are very smallish, and prevent you from actually pressing them easily. So... I removed the back half of the clam shell and cut off the button section (carefully)... and now its perfect. Not sure how good it will be if I drop it, but it does have the screen protector on the front. I probably won't buy this again unless I lose this one... cause I don't want to have to go thru the whole process of recutting the buttons out again.

text: I ordered this phone case from my iPhone6. I had a Lifeproof protective case on the phone that was wearing out quickly. The phone cover came promptly, fit well, and was as described. Very durable phone case and I feel confident it will protect my phone from my 15 month old who throws the phone frequently. The touch screen feature works without issue through the protective cover. While this case is moderately bulky it is not as thick as some other full protection cases I have looked into and considered purchasing. Easy access to the charging port and volume button. I love how vibrant the color is. Overall I am highly satisfied with this purchase and will likely order another one in a different color in the future. Highly recommend!
title: Easy access to the charging port and volume button

text: "360" means this comes with a rigid plastic back, a rigid plastic top and bottom that click into place, and an independent curved glass front piece. What it doesn't do is lock in that glass cover, so it really isn't all that different or better than other options out there. From the exploded view, I was under the assumption that the end result would be a more cohesive unit. The reason I'm giving it two stars is because the glass was not equipped to adhere all the way around the screen, so over four months, little bits of dust were able to get in under it, eventually affecting the adhesive. The glass popped right off.
title: Not great quality, unfortunately

text: This product did not work for me. The spring-loaded clamps on the sides did not hold well, My phone didn't fit into it very well and kept falling out. The support legs rested on my dash right where my controls for the clock and radio were so was always changing the time. It was difficult getting my phone set up in it when I wanted to use it. I called the seller and they immediately credited my card with the full amount. I'm giving the product a one star but Abco Tech a 5 star for great customer service. Thank for for making the return hassle free even though that item was not.
title: I'm giving the product a one star but Abco Tech a 5 star for great customer service

text: I'm not completely disappointed in this product. PROS: -good in length -nice weight in your hand -smaller tip, easier to use for precision -comes with replaceable tips (not sure if that's a good thing, maybe they are easily worn out. thats why they give you so many. i'm not sure) -easy to exchange the original rubber tip with a new one CONS: -color wasnt exact, pictured showed a metallic shimmer effect, which made the stylus appear lighter in color. i received deep dark solid colors. which isn't that big of a deal, it might be a personal issue. (had i known, i wouldnt have paid for them) -the rubber tips seem to be alittle too big for a "smaller tip" -when drawing, or writing you have to apply enough pressure for the device to read it, and by doing that you are basically dragging the excess tip behind you. if they made it a tad smaller it wouldnt be a big issue. other than that, i am content with my purchase, would i buy it again? no. its a good product, i am personally having too many problems with this specific item.
title: its ok.

text: I have a few GaN chargers but I think this is one of the best. It has a tiny light on the side of it to show it has power. It is labeled nicely so you know what to expect from it. The plug folds for travel. It is super compact for a 100 watt charger. It does not get hot. It comes with a high wattage cable which is great. There is a big difference in cables! Using a low wattage cable with a high power charger like this would result in less than stellar charging performance. The cable included is excellent! I tested charging wattage with several devices and all showed very high charge rate. I really like when manufacturers label their devices and cables with output or capability . This cable is labeled 100w so you know it can pass that much power and not confuse it with a lower power cable. It also has a light on it to confirm that it is charging. Nice! The cable is braided and super flexible. It comes with a Velcro strap to keep things tidy. This charger also comes with a removable travel adaptor for European plugs. Super nice and convenient for travel. It has plenty of ports and power to charge several devices at once. I cannot say enough good things about this charger combo! I highly recommend this!
title: I love this charger! Highly recommended!

text: I picked these up because they were advertised as compatible with the base Anycubic Mono, and that's *technically* true. These were clearly made for a cellphone, and compatibility with 3D printers was a happy accident. It covers the screen, but there's a bit of overhang that extends onto the protective tape that won't adhere. You end up with a lip along the edges that will catch resin in the event of a FEP tear and prevent the entire screen from getting ruined, but the edges will have a nice hardened trough as a result which isn't ideal. Yes there's bubbles that I couldn't remove, but those shouldn't affect the print quality. As others have said the protective film was difficult to remove, but rub your thumb across the edge a couple times and it'll come loose. It's better than nothing, but I'd have much preferred a product that was specifically designed for 3D printers.
title: Not intended for 3D printers

text: I hate to write a negative review for anything with Amazon's name on it, as I've enjoyed Amazon and their branded products greatly, but this product would be the exception. text: I am super picky and I love this case for my pampered iphone 4. Before I even get to the actual use of the battery, let me start by saying the fit and finish on this case is just superb. text: The mount is great. Period. I'm really looking forward to it being as tight as I want it to be. -- The magnets are really quite weak. Hence the 2 star. This is my third purchase of a magnetic mount (totally different brands) and this is by far the weakest magnet. I prefer to put the metal back inbetween my phone and my case (inside my case) and this magnet isn't strong enough to hold it. Other purchases of other devices have been almost strong enough but get a good bump in the road and it'll knock my phone off. This particular magnet, total mega weak sauce, absolutely not going to work for you if you're putting your metal place inbetween your phone and case. -- As a side note, I have some spare, old, dead hard drives, and I've remove the magnets out of them. Utilizing those magnets simply placing them on top of this magnet and then having those 2 magnets 'connect' to my phone, now it's strong enough and I have the mount I want. But alas, I continue the search for the perfect combination of mount and magnet. But again, this is definitely the best mount system I've used of the 3 I've purchased thus far.
title: The mount is great. Period

text: I own an legitimate Go-tcha, which I purchased from Game Stop. Decided to pick up another one for my husband. Unfortunately, what arrived was definitely a knock-off. (See pictures side by side with legitimate product). Differences: 1. Home button and display screen are smaller than on original Go-tcha (left side of my pictures). 2. Home button is dark red instead of bright red. 3. Fake Go-tcha does not have a lip/overhanging indentation under the screen. The original has a groove between the screen and he rest of the body, which the band can sit in and his is how it prevents itself from popping out too easily. 4. Different charger, larger than the original. The one I received doesn't actually charge the device! No charging screen is displayed when I charge and tap the fake, as opposed to the real one, which displays a charging screen. 5. Different wrist band. I received an all-white one compared to the red/white/black one with the real one. This is also a softer material compared to the stiff band with the real Go-tcha. 6. It doesn't work the same way. For the real one, I press the home button and it displays "GO-TCHA". For the fake, nothing happens. It won't event pair with the phone. TLDR; beware potential knock-offs that don't actually work! Mine was sold by "direct distributor".
title: Buyer Beware: potential knock-off!

Update to previous review: the band ripped apart at the seam after a few months. I had to sew it together to use again. Consider another band -- tune belt works great.

text: i just received this case in the mail, shipping was quicker than expected so i'm happy with that. however, there are some flaws i can see with this case. when i opened the package, the window for the nexus logo had slid down between the two layers of the case. now that it's on my phone it doesn't seem to wiggle around much but it's definitely not stable when it's off my phone. i also find that the power button is much more difficult to press, which is super irritating. the volume buttons seem to be doing fine. and if you're one of those people who find the textured power button on the nexus 6 to be a useful feature, you're going to have to get crafty and scratch it up because this case doesn't do that for you. and to top it off, the "free" screen protector doesn't fit properly on the screen. i do like that the case is lightweight and slim, it's not bulky or anything. i assume it'll protect my phone better than other cases that exist. the look of it is really nice- i love the logo cutout. i also really enjoy the dust protectors- i throw my phone in my purse often and, as all we women know, purses are the places of nightmares and horrifying things alike. so that's pretty cool. overall, considering the limited amount of cases available for this phone currently, this case is just very "meh". it'll do fine until i can find something better. A for effort, i guess.

text: Screen doesn't impact touch much. Slight reduction I'd say in top and bottom swipes. One of mine I could faintly see the touch dots in the plastic, the other I could not. text: This is a great phone. It has an amazing OS, and a great design. This is an amazing phone. It does work with At&t 3g if you are wondering, but I don't know about T-mobile. Pros: Screen- This phone comes with a four inch super amoled screen, which looks great. The colors are crisp, and blacks look like blacks. Blues look like blues, and reds look like reds. Colors look like they are supposed to be. OS- I love android, and think that it is better than Ios, Windows mobile, and blackberry. The app market has tons of apps, so don't be fooled by people who say that the Iphone has more apps, because it has all of the apps that you need. It is clean and smooth. Right now it comes with android gingerbread 2.3.3, but you get an update to 2.3.6, and the Nexus s has been confirmed to get the ICS update, and won't be long from now. Battery life- I charge my phone every night, but after using it for about 4 hours a day, using internet, texting, calling, and app usage, with auto brightness, I usually end up with about 60-70 percent of my battery left at night. Data Speeds- About 30 minutes out of New York, I get speeds of about 1 Mbps down, and .1 Mbps up which is fine for 3g. Cons: The only cons that I found was that this phone doesn't have 4g or a dual core processor. I'm 12 years old, so I don't need any of that stuff. Overall, I would definatly recommend this phone to anyone, especially since it will be getting the ICS update.
title: Amazing

text: I purchased Tech Armor for my SG3 after looking at the reviews (and the price, of course) and seeing that they were active on Amazon to try to improve their customers' situations. I liked that, and I do still like that about Tech Armor. For that reason, they get a few stars from me. As for the product, I just purchased a Zagg to replace my Tech Armor screen protector because I don't think that this product is all that great. For the price, you get your value I suppose. However, the protector scratches up and makes it hard to read certain spots, bubbles are pervasive, and by the time you use the card that comes with it to smooth out the bubbles, you've at least damaged the protector a bit. I would feel wrong giving this product a 5, because it is not deserving overall of a 5. The question that you should ask yourself is: do I want a bunch of cheaper screen protectors that last a shorter period of time, or do I want a few screen protectors that will last a much longer period of time? I won't say straight up not to buy this, but I would say that it wasn't worth my time having them constantly shipped to me and needing to be replaced. Personal preferences, I suppose.

text: Good for the price but it's a soft flimsy like plastic. Putting it in my purse it can get scratch marks from my keys or coins. The edges don't completely stick down to the curved phone and when I kept trying to push it down with my fingers the friction from rubbing it so much the film started having little bubbles in it. I'll deal with it for now until the bubbles really bother me or the film starts to lift up (since it's not fully sticking to the curved edge) I'll buy a different protector. It would look awesome if I had the Coral Pixel 4, but I just have the black. So far no scratches to either the case or my phone. I like how the case gives a lip to the camera portion so the bare camera is not resting on whatever surface I leave my phone. My biggest issue with the case is that the color both fades and looks dirty after a while. I've scrubbed, wiped, used different cleaners and soaps, but it doesn't seem to make a difference. I would describe it as more of a "dusty coral" now. I've had this case for about 2 months. Overall, it's a good price, but I might choose a different color next time.

text: I made the mistake of not reading the reviews about this product before purchasing. I just looked at the price and jumped. text: (1) The case is too slippery, especially the hard shell. Easy to get out of pocket, but also easy to DROP! A case that causes you to drop the phone is not very protective. (2) A bit of a pain getting the hard shell over the soft shell. (3) The cover on the charging port is protective, but an annoyance. (4) It is expensive. I bought the Otterbox because of its protective reputation. The case on my previous phone was a Spigen Tough Armour. It didn't have the Otterbox's 4 disadvantages. Maybe I'll get used to the Otterbox, but so far I like the Spigen better. Is the Otterbox more protective than the Spigen? Hard for me to tell.

text: This case is OK, however it is not an Otterbox, though it looks like it. It has a different, harder texture and the material is not as pliable as an otterbox. It is somewhat difficult to get the case on the phone, and off (in case you drop it in water and need to dry it, as I did last week.) A little difficult to get around the buttons on the phone, I was afraid I would break the case. The on button of your iphone is also going to get a little harder to press. text: Working great. Very transparent. Silky smooth feel as well. Bought for my wife’s 40mm series 5 and it works great. She’s super happy that her screen is protected now. For you 44mm owners... this is a must have for if you have the spegin tough armor case for your Apple Watch.. text: This case is very attractive and protective. It has a sliding section that covers the lenses of the camera to prevent damage, which is a nice feature. The 360-degree stand lets you position the phone for hands-free watching movies or FaceTime calls. The case fits very snugly on my phone - so much so that it was difficult to remove and when I applied pressure, it separated the soft inside plastic from the outside plastic on one side. With the case on, I tried to put the phone on my nightstand magnetic charging station, which sits at an angle from vertical. If I held it there, the phone would begin to charge, but with this case, the phone just wouldn't stick to the charger. If you have a horizontal pad you can lay your phone on, it should charge, but this won't work for my setup.
title: Won't hold on my magnetic charger; hard to remove

text: DO NOT BUY THIS! While sharp looking, the case is not well made. It is not sturdy as implied by 'Amazon Customer', as the top and button easily flex off the device as there is no plastic, just cheap tpu. Then there is the fact that the stand broke off the first day. I opened it to watch a video and it slipped off. Tried to put it back on and the part it clipped into was gone. I get it, it's cute and 10 bucks, but save your money and find another budget case, maybe a name brand for just a few $$$ more.
title: Wow... Broke on day 1

text: These cases look and feel nice and well made. I was very pleased with the first one I bought until I dropped it one day and it cracked at a weak point near my camera. In defense of the case, it did protect my phone, but it was not an intense fall that I would expect to cause a break. I assumed the first case breaking was a fluke, so I bought another one. Unfortunately, within several weeks the new one cracked in the exact same spot to the side of the camera after a modest drop. Since it is protecting the phone, I have continued to use it, but I am convinced that all these cases have a defect in their construction that cannot stand up to the occasional short drop.
title: Good Until It's Not

text: The installation went well, the use of the sticky strips for lint removal (from the phone and the "sticky" side of the protectors) is an excellent idea. I used the steamy-bathroom technique combined with the sticky-strips for the hinge application method (but the problem is they stick TOO well to the tempered glass and I had to re-apply it several times after learning how to peel the strips off without blowing the install. I'm very anal about removing all the dust and particulates to keep a clean application. However, a few days after installation, I noticed what looked like the rear screen protector on my desk, and lo and behold, it was the rear one stuck to a piece of tape that happened to be exposed. I was able to stick it back on with the aid of some eyeglass lens-cleaning solution, but of course there's a ton lint on the back now. I'll try taking it off and using tape to remove all the lint, but I doubt this will stay on, satisfactorily. As of now, the front screen is on pretty well, with some slight gaps around the corners where the S6 appears to start curving back, and the back is on with a ton of lint. Additionally, the front and back help make the S6 still smooth and slick without being so crazy slippery as it is right out of the box. Nearly a 4-star product. 1 more star for better application. 1 more star for the rear protection staying on.
title: Great, except back comes off too easily

text: I read the reviews before I bought this and some people were like for the iPhone 11 Pro Max be careful it doesn’t fit, blah blah blah. Maybe when this first came out there were issues or something with it, but I just got mine today and I installed it perfectly on my iPhone 11 Pro Max with the tray, and it looks literally perfect. There was no problem installing it, it fit very well, when I was about to pull the little sticker on the back after you let it sit for 30 seconds I was like wow that’s a lot of bubbles. Then I actually took it up off of the little tray and peeled off the protective coating and all the bubbles were gone LOL. It’s literally the easiest screen protector I’ve ever installed and I’m super excited about it!
title: Absolutely perfect fit for iPhone 11 Pro Max!

text: The look and feel of this gamepad is obviously trying to mimic an Xbox controller, and I think they did a good job of it. There's vibration support and also the buttons light up. I've tried it only with my Android phone so I can't comment on the compatibility with other devices, but it works with my phone well enough. My only complaint is that the phone holder is kind of small. I don't know why they don't just allow it to be extended a little bit further so it supports bigger phones. I have a Huawei 20x that I use to play games on, and it is too big to fit this controller.
title: Feels just like an Xbox controller

text: Overall this is a durable phone case. I have dropped my phone on asphalt 2-3 times already and my phone is just fine, minimal scratches to the edges of the case. The only thing I am disappointed in is the color is not as bright as pictured in the listing. I have the s20 fe and my friend ordered the exact same case for her s20 and it is as bright as shown. Just a stupid little thing but there are pretty much no purple cases that are actually protective for the fe. I don't use the holder/ring in the back and wish I could get it without, it catches on my work pants pocket. Overall great product and am happy with my purchase.
title: Good value, durable case

text: Installed the tempered glass as instructed..Pressed firmly center, slight outward in all direction.. firmly press on the edges, top and bottom...left over 12+ hours to settle down before putting on a case. I had to press really firm in order to launch an app. Also, the smooth and smear on the glass, it's really difficult to wipe any directions on the phone. Couldn't use the phone.. end up trashing the screen saver. need to protection on the screen but having to struggle to use the phone, it's worthless. very disappointing.

In the meantime I got her this set just to play around with and besides the 1st night exploring the set she has never once touched them again. You have to get the eye of the camera lined up perfectly over the lens and you also have to take your phones case off to use these. title: Maybe fun as a gift for kids??

text: I purchased this product because every other screen protector I have purchased does not stick around the edges of the curved glass of my screen. With the exception of the one that came on my phone from Samsung. I followed all of the instructions exactly. I even applied the product while in a steamy bathroom to reduce the amount of dust particles in the air. This product does not stick to the edges of the glass where is curved at all. I applied it like it said and even let it sit hoping that the edges would fall down over time but it did not work. I immediately pulled the product off and in my opinion it was a complete waste of money. Now I will be going to the mall and having the liquid screen protector applied for $25. The nice thing about that one is if it does happen to get scratched or something they will remove it and replace it for $5. I have already wasted over $40 and screen protectors glass and film type that do not conform to the edges of the screen. I don't know if the other reviewers were paid or not but it certainly seems like it. Because there's no way there's could have stick to the curved glass. By the way I live in the high desert in the temperature was about a hundred and six and the bathroom was even hotter which should have made the plastic film more pliable and likely to stick to the curve and it still didn't work.
title: Complete waste of time and money. GARBAGE

text: There's a lot to like about this screen protector, but it does have a major flaw. I haven't had any problems with the proximity sensor, but I was careful to keep the edge of the speaker cutout clear of the sensor. What really bugs me is how the screen peeks out from the sides. It's really bad with a white background (use dark mode everywhere you can as a work-around) because the edge of the protector creates a sparkly rainbow effect. I've seen pictures of other protectors that are too big and don't make a good connection because of the Pixel 3's curved edges. I'm hoping to find something better than this one, but for now it'll do.
title: Good install process, bad fit

text: I love this phone, always have. I loved everything about it. I could almost even text without looking. I've uploaded music onto the memory card so that it can play all of my favorite albums. Video, texting, call quality, everything.....except the bluetooth. It's faulty. It's not the software, it's the actual phone. Who cares about the upgrade, wow I get to pay $199 instead of the Fake $499 sticker price. I wish there was something I could do but there isn't. I even contacted LG directly and they were no help whatsoever. I'm great at fighting with companies to do whats right, but this has probably been my greatest challenge so far with a company. I don't really like any of the other phones available from verizon either so I'm kind of stuck. Hands free calling is going to be required by law in less then a month and I can't use my fancy Jawbone headset to do it... You've been warned.
title: Bluetooth Warning!!

text: Hard to apply. I had to do it twice. The edges won’t stick unless you press them down EXACTLY LIKE THE INSTRUCTIONAL VIDEO. I let it “dry” overnight as recommended and have no issues now. I use a tempered glass screen protector over this film (not pictured) but I wanted a secondary protection for when I’m not wearing a band with the tempered glass shell. Tempered glass over this film does not affect the touch sensitivity. I would rate it higher if it was easier to install. Good news is you can try over and over again with a single film and not waste one if you mess up like other protectors out there.
title: Tricky but effective

text: I have used Otterbox phone protectors for years. When you pay hundreds for a phone, you want the best protection from drops and other hazards. I am accustomed to the older version that had a cover for the screen. This was the closest I came for my needs, so while I have protection for the back and sides, I felt the need to have something for the front. The styling of this case allows for some overlap so if dropped, the screen will not have contact with the floor. The iPhone X is meant to be dust and waterproof, so I am guessing this is the reason for not including a front screen. However, the inexpensive glass screen protector I purchased helps with diminishing fingerprints. I have a hand tremor, and needed the case primarily for drop protection. I have dropped my phone several times without any damage.
title: Good investment, but no screen cover

text: For the past few years, I’ve had a regular phone mount for my Honda Civic. I’ve had to buy two replacements due to the lock and release contraption that holds the camera becoming stuck or defective. I’ve made do, but it was time for an upgrade. This phone mount, in short, is awesome! I don’t have to worry about my phone falling out of the mount, and I definitely don’t have to worry about it breaking anytime soon. It’s so cool the way it automatically opens and then automatically locks your phone in place. It’s also super convenient not having to plug in my phone when I set it on the dock. All in all, this is a must have. Now that I own one, I’ll never go back to a regular phone mount. It’s that kind of purchase! Enjoy one less hassle in your life for a change!
title: Feels Like a Need!

text: With my EVO I swapped batteries once or twice a day using a similar set up as this. It is rare to need to do this with my S3 but I wanted the capability. I do not notice a significant difference between these batteries and the original one. Though I've not tried to systematically compare them. They charge in the phone without any problem. In the charger it takes about 10 hours if they are fully discharged. Other reviews said it took a long time. But it was a surprise that I could put a battery in at bedtime and it was still charging when I went to work in the morning. Between having three batteries all together and knowing they need to start charging at dinner time rather than bed time is something I can work with. There was an issue once with the phone not turning on after installing one of the QCell batteries. I thought it may have discharged in my pocket, but it recharged quickly in the charger and was fine when I tried it again. It may have been pocket lint in the way or something. I only mention it in case someone else has had a similar issue.
title: Works fine. Charger takes a long time.

text: This case is amazing. It’s not to fat and bulky like I thought it would be so it’s very comfortable to hold. It also doesn’t make the screen hard to press, you won’t even notice the built in screen protector when using the phone with this case on. I do have some small complaints. The sound reduction is pretty bad. It’s hard to explain but if you set your phone down next to you or face it any direction away from yourself, you’ll notice the sound decreases. Obviously it’s because the case is waterproof and it has to cover everything but still.
title: Amazing Product , Small Issues Tho.

text: I got this screen protector earlier this week. I cleaned my screen using the included alcohol wipe and drying wipe. I got the protector to fit nicely where it should fit and air bubbles were pretty much non existent. The entire process took about 3 minutes with most of that being the cleaning of the screen. The bad part is that it lowers the sensitivity of the screen. Typing takes a little more effort and the double tap to wake up the now only works about 75% of the time. I'm highly considering just removing this from my phone. I don't feel like the protection makes the annoyance worth it.
title: Protects but inhibits

text: My phone is often confused with an older Galaxy S. As a T-mobile user, this phone seems to have no reception problems even though it always seems to show low signal strength. I have installed several apps and it works well with multiple of them running at the same time. Both cameras are decent, just remember not to move until after the capture sound or It will be very blurry. It occasionally freezes, sometimes when trying to unlock it, but restarting seems to fix it (note that I never turn the cellphone off). Overall, it's a good phone for its price.
title: Good for the price

text: So far it’s working fine except the Touch ID seems to be unavailable with this screen and the screen temperature is cool compared to normal iPhone color temperature which makes whites appear slightly blueish. That is the more annoying aspect. I would spend a bit more money to correct these two issues. So no, I can’t recommend this product and no I would buy it again. Update: my first day using this new screen and I have to add that the brightness level achievable is not as bright as an OEM screen and this makes it harder to see in daylight. Also the screen glass is more flexible than an OEM screen and appears warped when the light reflects off it. The finger print ID not working is a real turn off. Something I miss in the newer phones too.
title: Not OEM replacement quality.

text: I like the ability to cover the camera, so I am keeping the case. Case fits phone well. Kickstand works well, but I am concerned it will break off. It has little plastic pins it slides on in a track as you open and close it. My past experience with this design is that they break off. Also, I like to clean my phone with alcohol frequently. Alcohol takes the color off. If you put the case in your pocket and it rubs against other things like your pixel ear buds, the color rubs off onto the items in your pocket. The case does fit with my screen protector. I used a film protector. Wireless charging works. Unfortunately, there aren't a lot of case choices for the pixel that include a kickstand and are compatible with wireless charging.
title: Mixed review

text: I am now ordering my fourth case- this one for my wife. I have had two for my iPhone 6Plus. I eventually replaced it after the frame on the inner case split after many years of surviving many drops without any damage to the phone. The second case is still going strong but I replaced the phone with a 12 ProMax and bought a case for it. My wife paid almost $40 for her case from Verizon and the tempered glass screen saver is already broken so I'm ordering her the new case that comes with two screen savers for less than the cost of screen savers in most stores. I hate to sound like a shill for the company but this is a genuine bargain- you will not be disappointed!
title: Fantastic Quality, Durability & Price.

text: The leather smells amazing and this is some good thick quality leather. It’s nicely made and fits my cards and cash comfortably. Easy to access and remove cards and cash from slots. The design is what makes it easy and I love it because it looks nicer. It came with a small piece to test if it’s really leather. Fits nicely on my iPhone 14 pro max. The magnet is very strong and you really have to pull it to remove. Obviously it works well on my MagSafe charger. My only con is it doesn’t come in a variety of colors. I highly recommend this wallet and from seller.

text: By the time I get to post this, this will probably be in its 6 iteration. Saying all that, if anyone reading this considers purchasing one such as refurbished or used...DO NOT...I REPEAT...DO NOT. Call Quality has been horrendous since Day One when I purchased NEW. Namely people on the other end cannot hear you when holding the phone normally AND you will constantly need a microphone or Bluetooth earpiece to have any semblance of a conversation with the outside world. What saves it from being a total disaster is that it serves WELL as a mini-computer. Fairly Agile for the price (certainly better than a couple of older tablets I have). Camera is decent (not spectacular).
title: Please wait for the next year's model or look at other Budget phones.

text: It's an ok stylus, but I'm not sure why it is priced so high. Yes the nibs are replaceable but does that warrant a $30+ dollar piece of plastic and rubber? You can buy 10 styluses that work just as well as the price of this one. It's not well balanced. I kind of expected it to feel look and feel more expensive than it does. The casing is reminiscent of a Bic Pen. I found it didn't work so well on my Windows tablet and was a bit slow on the iPad. I had to use more pressure on it then i do with other pen styluses I own. Over all, I didn't find writing, surfing or sketching with it that satisfying. It would only work when the pen was at a slant, not perpendicular., which seems odd. Save your money, you can find the same quality for less on Amazon.
title: Overpriced for what it offers.

text: I recently bought the Apple Watch series 7 but hated the band that comes with. It irritates my skin after wearing it all day. I sleep with the watch on to track my sleep and it makes me wake up better in the morning as the watch vibrates on my hand so no more snoozing through my alarms. I love that as I’m trying to transition in being a morning person. I have a Fossil smart watch that I changed out the band to similar type to this and loved it. With the stainless steel band on my Fossil watch, my skin never got irritated. So, I knew I needed to change out my Apple Watch band. This was easy to change and so much more comfortable than the band that comes with the watch. It’s easy to adjust and it stays in place. No more pushing up my watch every so often as I didn’t want to go down a slot in fear of it being too tight but with this band I don’t have to worry about it. I can’t even fell the band, it’s so lightweight compared to the heavy band of the watch came in. It has an elegant look to it and it flushes nicely on the wrist with no gaps.
title: Lightweight & very comfortable

text: I am not sure why most companies are designing cases like this and leaving the bezels vulnerable to damage. The corners of the case are raised, but the sides of the case are not, you could still easily crack the glass of your phone if it falls on the right angle. Not sure I want to take that chance. Gesture navigation becomes a little more difficult when using a case with raised protection around the bezels, at least this is what I am experiencing now with the Falcon series case. I've been through 5 different case designs already, it hasn't been easy. -.-

The touch screen protector works well. The only downside which isn’t the case s fault is the charging port is too small for many chargers. The lightning cables that come with the iPhone fit fine. I got some 90* cables that don’t fit now. But it’s a small price to pay for the protection you get and the price. Deffinetely worth the money and would purchase again.

Everything slides in and out of the holster pretty quickly so you don't have to worry about missing a call because you ere trying to get your phone out. text: I bought a roocase for carrying my iPad Air around and love it, so I had high hopes for this case for my iPhone 6. I was looking for more protection and I loved that the screen protector was built-in. However, after using it for a while, it's clearly not what I had hoped for. Sometimes it wobbles when it sits on a flat surface, the flap to protect the lightning connector is stiff and hard to open and the screen protector is awful. I think it would probably provide better protection than some other cases, but it's defects are too annoying for me. Rats, guess the search is still on for me.

text: I followed the instructions what I thought was very well. At first glance the screen protector was smooth, no bubbles and great. Within a few hours it started peeling around the edges. I applied it again, made sure to clean the edges all around very thoroughly. Looked great at first, but within 24 hours it started peeling up at the edges again. The only thing I can think of is that the edges won't stay down if I use my case. Or maybe it just peels up because of the curved edges. Everything else was great, but it just won't stay on.

text: This IClever dash mount phone holder is a great and trustworthy product! Previously I had bought the iMagnet dash mount but ended up letting my wife use it and soon after just giving it to her. text: I bought this phone mainly because of the expandable storage offered by the microSD slot. I wanted a decent smartphone that would hold the dozen or so apps I use frequently, since the last phone I had used up half it's memory for internal functions. This phone seemed like a good option. And it was, for about a month. I bought it on July 29, I transferred my contacts, photos and apps, and I formatted my microSD card as internal storage. It went from an 8 GB phone to a 72 GB (64 GB microSD), and life was good. By August 24, the phone stopped acknowledging the microSD was in the slot. I tried taking it out and putting it back in, I tried cleaning it, I tried troubleshooting it by myself and with Motorola support, and nothing worked. My photos were irretrievably gone. Support and I both assumed the microSD was to blame, and I bought a new microSD and tried again. The brand new microSD that was recommended by Motorola support comes, and it too is not formatting to the phone. I spend a few hours on the line with Motorola trying to resolve the issue, and they manage to be perfectly unhelpful, asking me to go through the same troubleshooting protocol multiple times, and initially refusing to acknowledge that the phone, not the microSD was the issue. Finally, they relented and offered to fix the phone, if I mailed it in, leaving me phoneless for approximately a week. I called Amazon and told them the saga, and they offered me a full refund on the return. I replaced it with an Asus Zenpone. Based on how unhelpful Motorola was, I'll not be buying from them again.
title: Expandable storage fail.

text: Despite what the product listing says, these do not support fast charging. I tried them on multiple devices, all relatively new devices less than 2 years old each, and not a single device indicated fast charging was activated. Well, if the specifications printed on the bottom of the chargers are accurate, these are only rated at 1A for 5V DC output. Thus, they do not support the minimum amount of current necessary for fast charging at 5V (which would be at least 2A for any of the devices/specs I have ever seen). So, next I tried hooking up a resistive load that draws 1.5A at 5V to see what would happen. Within several minutes, the charger was getting hot to the touch. So since the desk I am testing on is not really setup to deal with containing anything if it got out of control, I cut that test short at that point. So it definitely needs to be kept under the specified max. That should be fine for charging any modern phone at slow speed. Thus these would be fine for having as an extra overnight travel charger for your suitcase/duffle bag, or as a replacement power source for a wireless charging stand that does not support fast charging. This would be a decent deal, but I deduct a lot of credit for my ratings, when the product information is just plain wrong.
title: Does not support fast charging on any devices I tried these on

text: I installed this booster in a less than optimal way because of the heavy snow on the roof at this time. The Yagi antenna is zip tied to the front porch post and the booster unit is mounted in the basement. The images shows a before and after signal reading. It's doing a great job and will probably do better when I mount the outside antenna on the roof in the Spring. Side notes: The outside antenna needs to be pointed at the cell tower your phone is using. It also has to be mounted vertically as shown in my picture due to polarization of the signal. There are apps that show what tower you are connecting to so you can point the outside antenna directly at it. The outdoor Yagi antenna is very directional and sends and receives in pretty much one direction. Because of this, you need to keep the indoor booster and antenna behind the outdoor antenna. The mounting plate is on the backside of this antenna.
title: +22 db signal improvement.

The movie features veteran actors Van Dyke, Rooney, and Cobbs in roles of old timer watchmen who offer Larry the job, and who we later discover are scheming for something bad; these roles are so silly for men their age, that they could destroy what's left of their legacy.
