text: This just arrived. A bit disappointed. Inner sleeve does not fit snuggly enough - phone keeps coming out of it. The sleeve has a nice feel and easy grip, but it is REALLY hard to get it to stay. Using the clip-on holster - it takes a bit to get the phone in and out of it, so you may miss a call, but the inner layer of the holster is a soft material, which is nice because that is what is coming into contact with the screen. That said, I bought this for my hubby as a Fathers' Day gift - he says he is totally satisfied with this and thinks I am rating it too harshly. It is a great price for what you get.
title: Takes some time to get it fitted properly...

text: After using this case, it feels like it's really overpriced. Granted, I didn't by their particular charging station because I have 4 of them and the Xvida charging station seemed absurdly overpriced. The 2 features that I was drawn to were the lightning cable pass-through port and the magnet in the case itself. The other cases that achieve qi charging on an iphone don't have a pass-through port and I've normally put a magnet or metal plate on the back of my phone to utilize magnetic holders in the car or home. The lightning pass-through port is great, and the only reason this review gets two stars. Some complain about no audio sync from the pass-through, but it didn't bother me. The magnet in the case is extremely weak, and seems to be concentrated around the edge of the square on the back. I put a metal plate back on the phone because the magnet didn't work very well. The actual qi charging feature doesn't work very well for me. Again, I did not purchase Xvida's charging station as I have 4 qi charging stations (none are Xvidas), but it only works on three of my four stations. Also, it's very particular about charging and will only charge if it's placed in the 'perfect' spot, like there's a sweet spot and only that one spot will allow for charging. I can also charge the phone for about 6-8 hours before it's at 100%. Very different experience from other qi charging cases. Quite unfortunate because at the high price point, I expected so much more.
title: Probably worth it at $15-$20 price point

text: I'll be honest I didn't expect it to work well. I was fully expecting to lose fingerprint reader functionality like with most of these protectors but that is not the case here. Everything still works which is very good! If you get bubbles during application but there is nothing stuck behind the screen, use a hairdryer to heat up protector a bit and push the bubbles out with your fingers. Overall installation took about 5 minutes and would have probably been even faster if it came with an installation frame. The only problem i have with this is that the black borders are a tiny bit too small and cut off about 0.5mm off the screen on the sides. This happens with EVERY SINGLE protector I've ever applied that have the black borders, including OEM once. I wish companies would stop dong this, the phone already has black border, you don't need another one. One last nitpick is that the adhesive layer could be a little thinner.
title: Works surprisingly well with the Pixel 7

text: Maybe I am just unlucky, but 2 out of the 3 protectors have cracked exactly the same way as pictured. The 3rd one I have not used yet, but I suspect it will do the same. Luckily when I lifted the glass there was no scratch marks or damages to the screen. The cracks appear to only be to the tempered glass, which is a good thing, but again 2 out of the 3 have cracked in the same manner at the edges and corners. Now this is isn't because I am reckless or careless. I have never dropped my phone once and only keep it in my pocket and desk. My Moto G7 Power is in pristine condition, behind the cracked tempered glass edges. Each time I have installed the screen protector cracks have appeared around the edges and corners after a few days of usage. Another drawback is that the tempered glass does full protect the phones glass. Around the edges are gaps.
title: Tempered Glass is fragile and cracks around the edges and corners

text: NO WHERE does the description state that you have to turn off the phone, remove the battery and let it sit overnight without touching it during the "application process". Had this information been available, I would not have ordered it. On top of THAT, application directions are not included. You have to go online to view the instructions. So.... If you are using your phone to go online to view the instructions, you have to memorize them or write them down before you can turn off your phone and remove the battery. I have owened many smart phones and never had an issue with my screen protector being scratched or othewise damaged and I have NEVER had to go through all this BS including spraying some kind of liquid on it. I feel this is extremely bad business to not provide the information about application on the product description. Not happy and will not be ordering from this company again. Thankfully I have Prime and can get another screen protector right away. Of course, I'm still out what this cost because I simply don't have time to deal with returning it.
title: NOT user friendly. No instructions incl. You have to turn off, remove battery, spray liquid on it and let it dry overnight.

text: Pretty much any case I've owned for my Iphone has had it's issues. The Otterbox I believe is the most over appreciated phone accessory ever, but the Speck Case for the Iphone 4 is a good earnest try at making a durable and sensible case. The one piece construction allows for the avoidance of all the stretching and warping that is characteristic of the Otterbox Cases. Other reviewers have complained about scratching. I personally see no issue, yes the case scratches, but the case is meant to be scratched- better than your expensive cellphone. The only issue I really had with the product was that the inner layer of plastic or rubber attracted dirt and browned. After time it also began to flake off like a pencil eraser. I have since upgraded to Iphone 5 and that Speck case and am happy to report that this problem has been largely solved as the rubber has been replaced with a harder version of itself. This case keeps the screen off the table top when facing down and is a great value for the cost and protection it provides. The best thing of all about it is my iphone still feels sleek because the case doesn't add much bulk to the form of the phone.
title: Great Case, Some Issues

text: I don't often use a pen or stylus on my iPad, but when I do I'll be happy to have this screen protector. It does double-duty: protecting your precious screen from scratches or smudges, while making drawing and writing on the screen much smoother. I can't verify that this actually feels like paper, but it is responsive to the movement of the pen. Several features make me recommend this set of three paper screen protectors. First of all, the video instructions are well-done and makes the process of adhering the screen almost foolproof. I accessed the video with the QR code on the outside of the package, but there is an option to find the video on YouTube. The 4-minute video has no voice or captions, but it is easy to follow and to pause to replay an action. Secondly, the package includes not only three screen protectors but all of the accessories for installing them, including a tool to smooth the protector and prevent air bubbles or creases. I advise watching the entire video before attempting to affix the protector, and then going slowly through the process. The video is very clear in demonstrating each step. Given my past experience with screen protectors for my phone and other tablets, I'm glad there are three included, just in case in mess up my first try. An important consideration is that this screen protector is designed only for the 10.2 inch iPads: the 7th, 8th and 9th Gen models. It will not fit the 10th Gen model with its larger 10.9 inch screen. I have the 9th Gen and the screen protector fits just fine.
title: A clever pen-friendly screen protector for iPad Gen 7, 8 or 9

text: First glass I installed had so many bubbles that I couldn't get rid of, I got frustrated and removed it to try again with the second one. The second went on better but I still had about 4 major bubbles. I applied pressure on each individual bubble for like 5-10 minutes each and eventually 3 went away. The fourth bubble on the bottom right corner was more stubborn and it took me literally 40 minutes of pressing it nonstop for it to finally go away. Now I have just one tiny bubble in that same spot just barely peaks out the black border that I won't mess with. The glass looks great and feels way better than the stock plastic it came with but I'm 50-50 about recommending it. I work for a cell phone company and have installed a couple of hundred glass protectors at this point so I know what I'm doing, it definitely was not me installing it incorrectly. So if you want to take the risk and have the time to be pressing out bubbles then I do recommend it.
title: It's quite nice but only if you're able to successfully push out all the bubbles

text: Bought the two-pack directly through Whitestone. Had used these protectors religiously on my Note 10+ with no problem. Had no problem installing the screen. text: I've been holding off writing a review until I had the chance to really break in the extended battery. The D3 is an undeniable battery pig. Before I had this battery I would be lucky to make it until mid afternoon before charging became essential. I'm hardly a power user and was disappointed in the stock battery performance to say the least. With this battery (following the instructions to fully discharge & recharge at least 3 times to break it in), I can make it through the entire day and into the next morning before charging is necessary. It's still not an acceptable performance but that blame lies firmly with the phone manufacturer. You'll need to download a battery monitor app to truly appreciate how much juice this phone drinks and to accurately track how far from empty you may be. The extended battery does make the phone fatter. What would you expect from doubling the stock capacity? I hardly notice the difference now but the hump on the back is not pleasing to the eye and causes the phone to bulge in your front pocket (especially if you keep a wallet in there too). Delivery was fast and the packaging looked more like something suitable to a Waterford Crystal vase. It's an excellent purchase if, like me, you experience serious anxiety when traveling or while away from a charger for any length of time.
title: Helps feed the battery pig

text: I bought two of these. Within the first two weeks one cracked. About two weeks after the other one cracked in the same spot where the volume button is. Then it got scuffed(?) in the back or something and now theres a dark spot and lastly a piece of the corner broke off. I've only dropped my phone once. Also note that these cases are very hard to put on/take off and if you use any type of clip mount the sides don't have any grip so the phone slides down. I wouldn't recommend these at all. I only give two stars because I liked the look and color of the case.
title: Low quality

text: maybe it is user error, but this is the second time that I have tried a skinomi on my smartphone, and I have ended up removing it and throwing it away. The video makes it look so easy to apply, but when I try it, I can't get the screen protector to slide on the screen such that I can properly align without getting air bubbles, even if I use a TON of solution. No more skinomi for me, unfortunately, unless someone can provide better directions or apply it for me haha. I fully acknowledge that it is at least partly user error, but it is hard enough that I have wasted two of them. Should it really be that hard for someone to apply a screen protector?
title: The video makes it look so easy to apply

text: Let me preface this post by saying I don't keep a cover on my phone, only a screen protector. I've never had an issue with broken screens, only scratched ones. I had been using a premium plastic screen from the manufacturer, but decided it was time to get a tempered glass to improve the tactile sensation on my figures when swiping. Unfortunately, I was disappointed in this product. After just a few hours, while treating the device very carefully, I noticed a small hairline crack across the screen. Shortly after the 24-hour mark, I noticed a light powder had formed in the middle right had side of the screen. After further review, it appeared as if the screen had started to disintegrate slowly. It was clearly a defect in manufacturing. When trying to pull the screen off, it came in many pieces. After my experience, I purchased a PThink 2.5D Round Edge protector and have been happy ever since.
title: Cracked On The First Day

text: This case looks great on the phone, it allows you to show off the design like it's nothing there and it will survive some decent falls but not a fall on the face. Shattered my screen with this case on it, I learned the hard way that it doesn't have a lip that extends the screen from the table/ground enough to consistently prevent shattering on a face down drop. I completely shattered the screen in one drop getting out the car. This phone is fragile, and expensive to fix the screen. What is $50-$75 on Iphone repair cost me $199; so just be advised, what you gain in minimalist design you may often give up in protection, when looking for a case!
title: Looks great but Not Very Protective.

text: I was worried about buying a phone case sight unseen, but after reading lots of reviews of various cases, I took a shot on this one. I love it! The case is slim enough, but still feels like it gives some protection (not as much as some other cases, but it's better than nothing), the power/volume button placement is perfect and the color is pretty accurate. I love that it includes the cutout for the Motorola logo, only because I place my finger on it quite a bit when I'm using the phone, especially when I'm on a call. Overall it's a great case and I'm very happy with it! An update for this review now that I've been using this case for awhile...I still love it! I've dropped my phone a few times now and the case has gotten slightly scuffed in some places, but more importantly, my phone is still fine. Granted, I've dropped it from a maximum height of about 4.5 feet, but it's landed on tile and asphalt and survived. I'm definitely going to try to stop dropping my phone so much, since I don't trust the case quite that much, but it's still holding up!
title: I love it! The case is slim enough

text: This little device is wonderful—great sound, quick recharge, well-packaged. And the seller got it to me a day sooner than expected! My only complaint is that I’m unable to turn the sound down low enough for my needs. I use an earbud as a sleep aid. The sound on my iPhone is set at the lowest possible setting while I’m using this little device. But the sound coming from this earbud is as loud as if I have the sound turned up to at least a quarter to mid-way of full capacity. If I try to turn it down any further, the sound shuts off completely. I’m so disappointed because this is a great product in all other ways. I will probably have to return it, if there is no other way to lower the volume. Any suggestions out there?
title: I’m so disappointed because this is a great product in all other ...

text: The Carbon Fiber Skin Protector is poorly designed. the skin for the front of the phone covers the front Camera, the light sensor and the status light. Also covers the Sprint logo. Instructions in the box are not clear about applying the carbon fiber cover - which has to be applied dry. The Screen protector has to be applied with the solution. Screen protector is great quality and according to Skinomi web site is highly resistent to scratching. I do no recommend this for the Sprint Epic phone. Expensive for a cover that is not properly designed for the phone.
title: Carbon fiber skin covers front camera, light sensor and status light

text: Main complaints: 1. The camera is crap (It's not a very expensive phone, so fair enough. This is the most minor of my complaints.) 2. The Bluetooth is constantly turning itself off permanently, meaning I have to RESET (not turn off and on but actually reset) the data/wifi/bluetooth to get the Bluetooth to work again. Happened 3 times in less than six months. 3. It just doesn't work very well. Example, if you're playing a mobile game or even just reading the news and get a phone call, the phone will continually ring but it will take what seems like forever for the answer option to come up, so you can't pick up the call. How frustrating. Sometimes by the time the button pops up, the other person has already given up or Voicemail has picked up the call. No, I'm not running a bunch of stuff in the background and my phone isn't full of bloatware. I understand that this is a budget phone, but my goodness, I shouldn't have to reset my phone every day to get standard features working. Save your money and invest in something better if you can.
title: The most expensive cheap phone I've ever bought

text: I LOVE the color and design but I'm horribly disappointed by this product. It's cheap so I can't be upset about the cheaply product but what I'm not happy about is it turns my phone off. If I want to use my phone it needs to be in the case and attached to the main wallet/case. If I take it off the magnet my phone turns off. I have to take the phone out of the entire case to use it or keep it in the wallet. Cards scratch the screen,glad I have a screen protector on Don't waste your money on this one. Spend a little more on better quality and functionality
title: Will turn your phone off!!

text: The strength of the magnet is pretty good, being able to hold my device, but the adhesive provided leaves much to be desired. You'd either need a perfectly flat surface or live in a cold climate (or both) because by the end of the week my mount fell off after I left my car in about 90 degree Fahrenheit weather (which isn't even the hottest my area gets at peak!). I have since then used 3M automotive adhesive to mount it and it's working pretty well. So overall with that being said, it didn't work too well out of the box for me, but it may work for you depending on your yearly weather cycle.
title: It's ok

text: Love the screen protector, the cutouts are precise and the 2.5d curve on the fingerprint scanner makes the glass feel very nice upon touch with no sharp edges. The screen when placed on looks very natural when paired up with a Orzly cause creating a natural look hiding the edges of the glass screen protector that hangs over the 2.5d edges on the phone. However, the reason I gave this a three star is due to the reoccurring problem in many 2.5d phone screen protectors. The middle glass is non adhesive so when the screen is placed onto the phone only the top, bottom, and sides adhere to the device. This creates a problem because in low light settings, usually dimmer yellow light settings, you can see the "oil slick" clear as day and it makes the device hard to use with this smudge in the way. The other issue is the dots in bright sunlight due to two reasons. One, the glass itself is very reflective so when in bright sun light the screen comes out dim especially on the Oneplus 3 due to its screen not being the brightest. Two the dots does not help with the already reflective surface as the dots make the screen even harder to see as the dots plague the entire screen clearly in bright sunlight.
title: Love the screen protector

text: I love these kind of cases for the protection the front lip provides for the screen should you drop it. I’ve never had a cracked screen when my phones been in cases designed like this. My issue with this model is that I’m unable to use the headphone jack with my l-shaped connection. The hole is too deep because of the case and I cannot push the headphone in far enough to make the connection. These cases aren’t designed to be removed constantly (the more your take them on and off the less secure the plastic snaps. Kinda sucks but if my headphones had a straight input I wouldn’t have an issue with it. Since they don’t, the case was sort of useless.
title: Great for drop protection, issues using accessories while phone is in the case

text: I purchased a Kindle last December along with the red lighted leather case. I absolutely love it and the fact that I don't have to carry an extra light around. The cover protects the Kindle and I have light whenever I need it. I often sit out back at night in my screened porch and am able to use only the light from the kindle,makes it so much more enjoyable than having the bright light glaring as I read. Also, its great for reading in bed as it doesn't disturb my husband. I think its worth its value. Am buying my Mom the package for her birthday in September.
title: I Love My Kindle and the Lighter Leather Cover

text: AmazonBasics Universal Air Vent Car Cell Phone Holder is an air-vent magnetic car mount holder for cell phones and mini tablets. It is extremely easy to use. My phone has a case so I removed the case and put the rectangular magnet in the case. I then put the case back on the phone. The phone can now attach to the magnet on the device that you slip into your air vent. It sets up in seconds and securely inserts into any dashboard air vent It allows for rotating device because the base stays in one spot. The kit includes 2 magnetic plates. One small round plate if your phone does not have a case and one larger rectangular plate for a device with a case.
title: Magnetized phone holder works well

text: Installed this battery in daughter's 18-month old G6 since I was doing surgery anyway on the screen. It came with a goodly number of tools, however, I still think you'd need a heat gun to get the back cover off (heat gun *not* included with the battery) and the spudger and suction cup supplied would never let you get the back cover off unless it had been off previously. I used an iFixIt suction cup from a previous repair on a different phone which worked much better than the suction cup included, as well as some strips of hard plastic from clamshell packaging to get between the back glass and the midframe. The battery is perhaps 4 mm shorter than the OEM, but this may simply be the packaging around the power lead/charging circuit. The battery came with self-adhesive strips and it connected properly to the motherboard of the phone. It would only charge to an indicated 86% initially, however, after performing a "battery reset" (Google it) the charge indicator started working properly. The phones been through about 4-charge/discharge cycles and the new battery seems to be doing fine. I'd buy from these folks again if I needed another battery for another phone. I'd like, however, to be able to buy just the battery and save the expense of the tools I'll not be using.
title: Maybe a Hair Shorter than the OEM - But it Works Fine

text: Loved it in the beginning! I didn’t like the idea of committing an adhesive ring to my phone. The magnet has a decent hold, but does pop off easily depending on the way I’m hold the phone. The ring has become very loose over the few months of using, to the point that I can hear it flopping against my phone when it’s in my pocket. Using as a stand was amazing initially, but do to the loose ring, I no longer can get the phone to stand up unless the ring is fully extended. Great product in the beginning, “meh” product now.
title: Floppy ring after a few months

text: This was in storage for a while as I had bought 2 different covers. I just put this on a couple of weeks ago. It's sleek and looks great. While it protects the phone from drops, not the same can be said of the cover itself. The first week it fell on the upper spine cover and cracked a corner. The second week it fell on the carpet and the opposite corner away from the spine broke off a 3/8" diameter. You'll love it if you only use your phone sitting on a desktop. Not very practical for daily use.
title: A Mess Within A Couple of Weeks

text: I called BLU the other day to find out how to get my phone fixed. I went through all of the problems in detail with their agent. And the only response I got was to do ANOTHER hard reset on the phone to original factory settings! This is irritating because I have done this on the phone twice already. And each time I reset the phone, I loose all of the information and applications that I previously loaded on the phone. Does BLU honestly believe that I have time to reset my phone, contacts, applications, etc., each and every time? My BLU Life Play 2 is junk! - The camera has failed twice, ... which is why I know about having to do the hard resets. I did this twice to recover use of the camera. - The power button on the side does not recover the phone from standby. - The screen flickers. - There is an area in the lower corner of the screen, approximately 1/2" x 1/2" that is much brighter than the rest of the screen. - The phone's Bluetooth will sync with my car, but I have no access to the contacts on the phone. This is the case with the other two BLU cell phone we have, too. I have asked about a full refund since the phone is still under manufacturer’s warranty, or to have it replace. But, this will be the second replacement since I originally purchasing a Life Play 2 in October 2014. So, there is a lot of hesitancy about getting this phone replaced … especially when customer service is so poor. I am NOT happy at all.
title: BE VERY CAREFUL ABOUT BUYING ANY BLU PHONE!

text: The bracelet is attractive, seems to be well made, and fits on the fitbit nicely. I had to remove a link from each side to size it to my wrist, and the instructions to do so paired with the provided tools made it a breeze. From opening the box to on my wrist was about 15-20 minutes. Durability is yet to be seen (I've only had the bracelet for 3 days at this point) but thus far I'm very pleased. It adds a nice weight to the fitbit that was lacking with the stock rubber strap and other aftermarket straps I've tried. I have the black fitbit on the plain stainless bracelet and the color contrast looks nice.
title: Attractive, well-made bracelet at a great price

text: The same day the Selfie Stand arrived I proceeded to test it by mounting my iPhone 7 Plus and GoPro. I even tried my Nikon DLSR camera though understand this stand/tripod is not designed for heavy cameras. The first mistake I made was I kept twisting the fitting and ended up pulling the top pole out. Two clear plastic pieces fell out but I managed to put them back and reinsert the pole back. Whew! My iPhone 7 Plus fit just right in the clamp. And same for my GoPro fitting just right on to the adapter. I then went on to connect my phone to the Bluetooth remote. I contacted the seller and they promptly sent me a replacement remote -- Actually they sent me a universal flexible tripod with remote and GoPro adapter! I am one happy customer. Great customer service!
title: very happy

text: I got this for my 15yo and it's going back if it can. First, he dropped it one time and a corner of the case cracked off. text: This is definitely not something for mobile use - it's heavy, really requires clipping to a table of some sort, along with the need to plug into a USB for power. I initially tried clipping it at a higher angle on the top of monitor but that configuration didn't work as the arm holding my phone would just fall. This doesn't happen when clipped horizontally on my table. That being said, I like the lighting options, very easy to use (buttons to toggle on/off, adjust brightness, and change between 3 light options). I don't have a lot of natural light in my apartment so doing instagram stories or videos has always been a combination of creative timing for sunlight or getting close to my desk lamp. This product provide ample light for taking videos or pictures, even in the dark.
title: Great Light, Heavy, Lacking Some Versatility

text: This is a pretty good screen protector. It was easy to install with absolutely no bubbles or problems. Perfect fit for my Galaxy S5. really smooth and creates minimal fingerprints and when it does it easily wipes with a microfiber cloth.(all I use on my devices) Reason for two stars................? It arrived promptly, but was poorly packaged. In a plastic case inside a bubble envelope. when opened the plastic case was broken/cracked. This started my worry process. Upon opening the case(I had to break it entirely to get into it) I found the screen protector intact, but with a crack at the bottom between the outer edge and the start button hole. Maybe a minor annoyance, but there just the same. I did not file a claim with Amazon, Just too much trouble for such a small item. Not worth the hassle to go through the return, replacement, refund process. The screen protector was shipped via USPS. That may have been the biggest problem right there! Outside of that, if you receive the screen protector in good shape, I think you will be well satisfied with your purchase.
title: Broken!!!

text: I ordered a 256GB iPhone XS on a Thursday to replace my 64GB iPhone 8. I received the “Renewed” iPhone on Monday. Cosmetically, there is a very slight scuff on the back which is barely noticeable. There was a small sticker with a barcode on the back that was very easily removed. The screen already had a glass screen protector installed. Long story, short, someone loved this phone. Battery life was 84%, and it holds a charge. I backed up my iPhone 8 through iTunes, then updated iOS on the new phone before restoring. Seamless. I’d very much recommend buying one of these vs. full price.
title: Two thumbs up.

text: I purchased this case because I really liked the case I had for my Galaxy S4. That case was sturdy, well made, and protected the phone well. However, I'll be returning this case for a couple of reasons. First, the construction was poor. The rubber part of the case is misshapen in a couple of key spots. The bottom cover for the lightning connector will NOT stay closed. There are large gaps all around between the rubber and the plastic. And the rubber doesn't seem thick enough in key areas like the corners. I'm certain that if I dropped my phone on one of its corners with this case, it would be damaged. Second, this case made my phone over TWICE as thick! It's difficult to get in and out of pockets unless your pants are really baggy. Yeah, the wallet feature is pretty neat, and that's the main reason why I chose this case over any others. But it only holds a couple of things, and that's not enough to make it worth the extra hassle.
title: Poor Construction

text: Fitment is good, tight and low profile case to add a bit more protection to an already durable phone. Back of the S7 active has a nice textured finish that makes the phone easy to one-hand... This case is much more slippery. Unfortunate though the phone is now more protected, it feels more likely to be dropped. And my main issue, I ordered red. This is not red. This is pink. My phone is pink :/ Edit: after asking my friends, I think this may be a case (no pun intended) of the gold/white dress vs black/blue dress. Some people say it looks red others say it looks pink. It may have to do with lighting. Since the case is transparent, in bright light it looks lighter and pinker. In dim light it looks a lot more red
title: Pink not red

text: In the past 10 years, I've owned many smartphones. I've protected my investment every time with screen protectors, and have completed successful installations thereof dozens of times over. This screen protector proved no more challenging than any of the others, but the quality has proven to be vastly inferior. Within 6 hours of applying it to my Galaxy s8 plus, giant bubbles had formed, the touch surface was "clicky" as the adhesive was not strong enough to continue holding to the surface of the phone, and within half an hour of noticing those issues, it fell right off my phone with no force whatsoever. Now I've got to reorder, take the time to return this junk, and deal with no protection for my phone in the interim. Learn from my mistakes and browse elsewhere.

All in all, great product for the price.

If you're on the fence about ordering, you will not be disappointed with this case. I would highly recommend it.

text: While this cell signal booster does do a decent job of boosting the signal and supports a decent amount of cellular bands, it will not fix really bad signal quality. It can help some because it does have a larger more powerful antenna to send and receive from compared to a cell phone. If the signal is bad because of distance or other obstructions, then even the better antenna cannot always help that much. This has a very simple display for troubleshooting and setup on the device itself and it would be nice to see a display with more information for a cell booster at this price.
title: As with other signal boosters, bad signal quality is still not great even after being boosted

text: Holds both the phones with hard case note 5 and note 8 fine without falling out and is size adjustable, but since the base doesn't have any suction underneath the whole thing gradually moves all over if you run into road bumps or pot holes or even minor road damage. It's like you have to keep an eye on it, if driving on uneven roads. And avoid it if you have a fast n furious driving style. Also, if your dash is not perfectly flat or inclined upwards towards you, it'll be difficult to view the screen if it's used for navigation. text: For the price, this phone does what it's supposed to do; be a phone. You can get calls, send texts, etc... The screen is large and actually has very good picture quality, so it's great for watching movies and YouTube videos and the like. The issue with it is that it's so unbearably slow and laggy. With a 1.2GHz processor and 1GB of RAM, this device runs horrible under any sort of higher workload. You must constantly end tasks and even force quit apps that don't want to close. Also, the device is not 1:1 compatible with all apps on the Play Store, so you will find that a lot of apps do not work at all on this phone. Despite the negative, it is a very decent phone for the price. I personally bought it when I was denied a replacement after my old phone broke about a year ago, and I've had it since. Just don't expect a S7 Edge-similar experience.

text: My previous headset was a Jawbone Era, which I liked a lot, but found uncomfortable when wearing for long stretches. My Bose SE2 headphones were very comfortable and good quality, so I thought I would try a Bose bluetooth headset. The headset is very comfortable to wear all day, but it's far from perfect. My main gripe is the size. The thing is always leaning down and feels like it is going to fall out of my ear at any time. It doesn't, but it will make you paranoid about losing the device. The second problem is that the volume just does not go high enough. When using it to listen to audio podcasts, I can't hear a thing if people are talking in the same room as me. I love it, but I do hope there's a Series 3 in the future that addresses these concerns.
title: Better, but not perfect

text: Ever since we bought stand-up paddle boards last summer I've wanted a way to take my iphone with me and protect it. I also want to be able to take pics of the family on the boards. I was nervous about offering up my expensive phone to a plastic sleeve so I did a tissue test before using it and it passed with flying colors. So last weekend was our first trip to the lake this summer and it worked beautifully. My phone stayed dryand I was able to text and take pics easily. The pics and videos were clear. My iphone with a regular case fit great. The closure mechanism is tight and secure. Thanks for a great product! I received this item at a discounted cost in return for an honest review.
title: Great protection in the water!

text: I’m editing my earlier review. Now that I have had this for several months and got used to it, I’m quite pleased with it. With a different brand that I had before, I found myself replacing the protector often because it would crack so easily. With this one, the first one I put on is still going strong several months later. Even after many drops. My eyes did get used to the clarity issue quite quickly and I do not notice that it is any less clear anymore. I would purchase again! I’m a bit disappointed to be honest. I just received mine and put on my new phone. I had another privacy screen protector on that was too small from my previous phone while so waited for this one. I took the other off and put this one on immediately and the screen is noticeably less clear to me. It must be the cross hatching to make the privacy. I may get used to it, but this was not a problem with the other company I had, but they unfortunately don’t yet have a screen protector available for the iPhone 13 pro. This does feel pretty nice and covers every bit of the screen, but I wish it was clearer to read the screen. I also don’t think it offers as much privacy coverage on the angle as it advertises. Sure it’s darker, but not the blackout it has pictured. I wouldn’t buy this one again. I’ll likely search for another.
title: Editing my earlier review…pleased with this after several months of use

text: This case is exactly what I need. However, it does add some bulk and weight to the phone. If your phone gets dropped often, this is the case for you. The only reason it doesn't get 5 stars is because of the screen protector. I can never get it completely clean and I think the resolution could be better. Also, the covered outlets take some getting use to since I need access to them daily. I have the Otter Box Defender cases for my iPad and iPhone. They do add bulk and that's why I initially would not purchase them, however after dropping my equipment a few times, I changed my mind. It feels great to know I'm unlikely to harm my phone when it's dropped. With this case, "it takes a licking and keeps on ticking."

text: More like 3.5 starts. It didn't come off as 'elegant' as some previous reviewed praised but it is doing it's job. I like it but wish the flap was built differently. When it sits closed it leaves a few mm's of space i wish it covers. I feel it will get worse over time, but too soon to confirm/be certain. Will update if anything mindblowing happens.

text: I bought this case about a month ago and was inadvertently shipped two... Good thing because they're a tad delicate. The first one broke when I removed it to add a sim card on my phone so, luckily I had the spare which lasted until I removed it to try on a different case... Boo. Additionally, the pattern faded quickly from the corners so it's starting to look cheap and would need to be replaced anyway. Other than that, I love the feel of it - it's got a nice grip to it. All in all, it's just OK - I guess you get what you pay for.
title: Just OK

text: From one customer to another, do not buy this case. I don't know what they were thinking, but the choice of materials in designing this case is awful. Allow me to explain: the case is primarily constructed of a relatively stiff matte plastic with bits of rubber on the sides and corners. The issue here is this stiff plastic, as it has a matte texture that is constantly in contact with the delicate glass back of the note 7. After a few days of usage with my phone, I noticed some scuffs and abrasions on my phone that were caused by the harsh plastic rubbing against it. As for all the other aspects of the case, it works decently. Nothing is notably terrible, but I can't overlook the glaring fact that this case is ironically causing damage to the phone it's supposed to protect through the abrasive plastic damaging the glass surface of the Note 7. Overall, I will be returning this case. Bottom line is that for $40 at the time of this review, this really isn't worth it if the material of the case actually damages my phone instead of protecting it.
title: This case will cause scratches and scuffs to your phone

text: It’s a great product if you don’t drop your phone. Protection is so limited. No screen cover like the defender. In a nutshell, if you want something fancy, go for the commuter, but if you want real protection for your phone, the defender is the best. I had the defender first and thought it was too bulky so I got the commuter. But now I’m always panicking about leaving my phone anywhere / my phone falling/ resting anything on it. I didn’t have that worry with the defender. If you can imagine a soldier inside a tanker, that’s how my phone was inside the defender. The commuter does not offer much protection especially for the screen. No screen protection.

text: I'm a long time user of Otterbox products. I had it for the 4s and my 5. I recently got my iphone 6. I used my phone without a case for about a week and a half before I got this case. The screen protector does not sit flush on the Iphone screen. This causes trouble with typing, scrolling on pages such as facebook or instagram, and sliding between your home pages. Like a lot of other have stated, you have to REALLY mash down your volume buttons. Ive had a little difficulty with the power button, but not as bad as the volume buttons. Otterbox really needs to come out with a 2.0 version of this case and offer everyone who purchased this case a refund or an updated version. Aside from these problems, I feel like my phone is well protected, like what you would expect from Otterbox. However, functionality is not something that should be sacrificed to protect the phone. I'm not a clumsy person (knock-on-wood), I'll be going without the case for now. Just upset i dropped nearly $40 on something that doesn't work like it should.
title: Don't buy

text: This strapped on my arm nicely and did not slide. Touch screen was a little harder to work but I have a screen protector on also. The reason I said to read that it was for an IPhone was because I have a Galaxy Note 9 which has the same dimensions as one IPhone model. However, the cameras do not go down one side of the phone. They go across so this completely covered them. Having said that, I have yet to find anything that accommodates those cameras. I believe Samsung has gone back to the usual design since that year. If I had the IPhone so it fit it would probably be a constant companion. The only thing I have realized is that no matter what camera you have, in an emergency you need time to get the phone out of the sleeve which has a couple layers to get through. Living in the city, that is the one thing that would make me hesitate.

text: The case itself is well made and looks very good on my phone. The biggest problem I have with the case and the reason it's no longer on my phone is that it is NOT compatible with screen protectors. The sides of the case kept digging under my screen protector and causing it to pop off the screen. text: It's not like I don't know what silicone feels like, but I read elsewhere that it wasn't the tacky kind of silicone and so I had high hopes for this silicone case for my iPhone 5. I wanted an orange case, and this one is a nice orange. The color in real life is very bright and pretty. However, the texture is soft and gummy enough that it picks up dust and lint, and doesn't have enough structure to provide much protection. The case comes with two screen protectors, which was thoughtful, but they are shiny instead of matte, and fingerprints show easily. I'd prefer a more protective case with a less gummy texture, plus a matte screen protector. So I will look for replacements for both of these. However, this will do for basic protection until I find something better.

text: I have used these screen protectors before and love them, but just got a new phone so i had to get new ones. for some reason, both the ones i received have small little bubbles around the sides, where the matte part ends and they don’t go away with pressure as if there was air trapped under there. I didn’t have this problem with the last ones so maybe just got a bad batch? They also seem to be a bit misshapen, coming in a bit on the long sides which made it hard to line up correctly. Again, overall i really like these screen protectors but am a bit disappointed with the ones i got.

text: After reading a bunch of reviews on how to install this film cover I was nervous about doing it myself. However, I must say that the video was very helpful and the hinge method works great! Did I get a speck of dust underneath the film? Yes. Is it horrible and intolerable? No. I actually had 3 phones that needed this film so I had only one shot for each of them. The first one I did get two dust specks underneath but again, it's not noticeable to me. The second one I got one tiny dust speck but thankfully it was at the top of the phone and not a problem. The 3rd phone was perfect! I would definitely recommend this film. I had been very nervous about using my phone w/out the protector - afraid I'd scratch it or crack it. With the film in place I don't worry about it. I also bought a Cruzerlite case which fits like a glove so I'm all protected!

text: Tonight I left my phone on top of the trunk of my car when I refueled the car. Then I drove back home and it fell off when I turned left at the crossroad. After half an hour I located the place through "find my iphone" app. My iPhone was lying in the middle of the road. It got pretty dirty and had many scratches on the case but except for a small chip on one of three lens, there is no other damage on my phone! It is quite possible quite some cars have driven over it during that half an hour, not to mention that it fell off in the middle of driving! My previous iphone cover was much thicker than this one, however, after several drops, the back glass of the phone was heavily broken. This one looks not very thick, however, it protected my phone so well. Not only this time, I dropped my phone to the hard floor multiple times before, the phone had no demage at all. I highly highly recommend this case. I normally don't like to write a review to praise something. For this case, I not only bought a new one again but also write this review to express my thanks.
